**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig OPC UA, client and server, allocation-disciplined and I/O-free (byte-in/byte-out server state machine, caller-driven clock) and MIT where the C/Rust references are MPL and the Python one LGPL; secured server (`Basic256Sha256` Sign/SignAndEncrypt) verified against open62541 binaries and asyncua. **Where we are behind:** events/alarms and monitored-item filters, HistoryRead, node management, newer security policies (`Aes128Sha256RsaOaep`, `Aes256Sha256RsaPss`), X509/Issued identity tokens, PKI trust store, full standard NodeSet, PubSub (→ Backlog items).

## Design & invariants

- **Layered, each layer independently testable:** `encoding` (OPC 10000-6
  §5.2) — the built-in type codec over a `std.Io.Writer`/`std.Io.Reader`;
  `transport` (OPC 10000-6 §7) — the opc.tcp handshake and MSG/OPN/CLO chunk
  framing over a caller-supplied stream; `services` (OPC 10000-4) — the
  request/response structures and the client-side `Channel`; `security`
  (OPC 10000-7) — the Basic256Sha256 secure channel; `nodestore`
  (OPC 10000-3) — the server's address space; `server` — the server-side
  connection/session/subscription state machine; `root` — the client's
  `SecureChannel`/`Session`/`Subscription`.
- **Every structure is bidirectional.** Each Part-4 message has both an
  `encode…` and a `decode…`, which is what let the server side be built
  without duplicating a single line of codec: the server decodes exactly the
  structures the client encodes and vice versa.
- **Transport-agnostic, no socket ownership, no timer ownership.** The client
  takes a reader/writer pair. The server takes *bytes* and *a timestamp*:
  `Connection.feed(input, out, now_ms)` and `Connection.tick(out, now_ms)`.
  There is no thread, no `std.time`, no socket anywhere in the module — the
  Linux poll loop that drives it lives in the test file
  (`server_interop.zig`) as an example, not in the library.
- **Little-endian, unlike this repo's other binary protocol codecs**
  (`snmp`'s BER and `coap`'s options are big-endian): OPC 10000-6 §5.2.1
  mandates little-endian for every multi-byte scalar. A deliberate
  divergence, not an inconsistency to "fix".
- **Address-space ownership: the store owns every byte it holds.**
  `nodestore.addNode`/`setValue`/`writeAttribute` deep-copy their arguments
  with the store's allocator, allocated exactly the way `encoding.Decoder`
  allocates so `encoding.free*` frees them. `readAttribute` borrows, and is
  documented as valid only until the next mutation; anything that must
  outlive one (a monitored item's last-reported value) deep-copies via
  `dupDataValue`.
- **Per-request arena on the server.** Every inbound message is decoded, and
  its response built, in an arena that dies with the message; only long-lived
  state (sessions, subscriptions, retransmission queues, continuation points)
  uses the server allocator with explicit frees. A malformed request
  therefore cannot leak: the arena is released either way.
- **Error policy:** malformed wire input becomes a typed
  `EncodeError`/`DecodeError`/`TransportError`, never a panic. On the server,
  a malformed *service body* becomes a `ServiceFault` (the connection
  survives), while a malformed *framing/limit* violation becomes an `ERR`
  message and a closed connection — the split OPC 10000-6 §7.1.4 describes.

## Design notes by feature

- **Client-side SecureChannel renewal.** `SecureChannel.renew(now_ms, options)` (`root.zig`) sends
  `OpenSecureChannel` with `RequestType = Renew` (OPC 10000-4 §5.5.2) on the open channel: same channel id, policy and
  mode; at Sign/SignAndEncrypt fresh nonces are exchanged and the keys re-derived (P-SHA256, §6.7.5).
  `renewalDue(now_ms)` (`root.zig`) / `renewIfDue(now_ms, options)` (`root.zig`) time it: **75 % of the revised
  lifetime** (`renewal_fraction_percent`, `root.zig`), **but not sooner than `min_renewal_delay_ms` (50 ms,
  `root.zig`) after the token arrived**; a revised lifetime of 0 is refused with `error.InvalidTokenLifetime`
  (`services.zig`), and with no lifetime (`token_lifetime_ms == 0`) nothing is ever due. References: open62541's
  client sets its next renewal to 75 % of the revised lifetime, node-opcua clamps its timer to `max(75 %, 50 ms)` (read
  as behaviour only). One deliberate difference: they count from the server's `CreatedAt` or a local timer; this module
  has no clock (`meta.platform = .any`), so the caller passes a monotonic `now_ms` to `open` (`OpenOptions.now_ms`,
  `root.zig`) and `renew`, and the deadline is counted on that local clock, immune to server clock skew. The new
  token and keys take over the moment the answer is read (what both references do); the server keeps accepting the old
  token for `token_renewal_overlap_ms`, capped at its own expiry, so a request in flight is not cut off. A refused
  renewal (a Bad answer, an answer naming another channel, an empty server nonce at a secured policy, a failed
  signature) leaves the old token, keys, lifetime and install time untouched, so the caller can retry while the old
  token lives; renewing a channel that was never opened or was closed is `error.InvalidSecureMessage` before any I/O.
  The client has one request in flight at a time, so `renew` is called between requests.
- **Client-side subscription and path services.** `Subscription.setMonitoringMode(mode, item_ids)`
  (`root.zig`, §5.12.4) and `Subscription.modifyMonitoredItems(specs, timestamps)` (`root.zig`, §5.12.3, no
  filter, like `createMonitoredItems`) and `Session.translateBrowsePaths(paths)` (`root.zig`) are the raw services:
  one result per id / item / path (a stale id or a path that matched nothing is a Bad entry, not a failed call; an empty
  list is the server's ServiceFault, kept on `Channel.last_service_result`), and the caller frees the response with
  `services.freeSetMonitoringModeResponse` / `freeModifyMonitoredItemsResponse` /
  `freeTranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIdsResponse` (`services.zig`). The shape follows open62541 (the generated
  service call, results as the server sent them); a one-path convenience is left to callers. `MonitoredItemModifySpec`
  (`root.zig`) carries the `ClientHandle`, because the spec puts it into the modified parameters and our server
  stores it: the `monitored_items` correlation table follows the new handle for every item whose result is not Bad, and
  a Bad result leaves the entry as it was. `setMonitoringMode` keeps no local bookkeeping (the client table does not
  track the mode).
- **Per-policy RSA key-length band.** `SecurityPolicy.minAsymmetricKeyBits` / `maxAsymmetricKeyBits` / `allowsKeyBits`
  (`security.zig`): 2048..4096 for `Basic256Sha256` and the reserved `Aes256_Sha256_RsaPss`
  (`Aes128_Sha256_RsaOaep` has the same row but is not an enum value here; `Basic128Rsa15`/`Basic256` are not
  implemented, so their 1024..2048 row has nothing to attach to). Checked on the modulus length read from the
  certificate's structure (`security.certificateKeyBits`, `security.zig`, over `rsa.PublicKey.modulusBitsFromDer`)
  before the key is parsed, so the answer is the same under every build profile. Enforced on the peer certificate key
  (server `checkPeerCertificate`: `BadCertificateUseNotAllowed`, what open62541 answers from `rsaNewChannelContext`,
  256..512 bytes; client `SecureChannel.open`: `error.KeyLengthOutOfPolicy`) and on the own key (server: OPN refused
  `BadSecurityPolicyRejected`; client: the same error; `generateSelfSigned` with `modulus_bits` out of band:
  `error.KeyLengthOutOfPolicy` before any prime search). One deliberate difference from open62541: the band is on the
  exact bit length (the spec text), not `(bits+7)/8`, so a non-byte-aligned 2041..2047-bit modulus is refused here and
  accepted there. node-opcua documents the same 2048/4096 rows. Testing escape
  `insecure_allow_key_length_outside_policy` on `GenerateSelfSignedOptions`, `SecurityContext` and `SecurityConfig`
  (`security.zig`; named after rsa's `insecure_allow_small_modulus`); under it a key past the build's RSA
  capacity still cannot be used (`BadCertificateInvalid`).
- **NumericRange** (OPC 10000-4 §7.27). `numeric_range.zig`: `parse`, `Range.format`, `Range.init`, `readRange`,
  `writeRange`; the server applies them in the Read handler and `NodeStore.writeAttributeRange` (`nodestore.zig`);
  the client sends one with `Session.readAttributeRange` / `writeValueRange` (`root.zig`) or any
  `ReadValueId.index_range` / `WriteValue.index_range` string. Spec first; open62541 (`UA_NumericRange_parse`,
  `checkAdjustRange`, `UA_Variant_copyRange`, `Variant_setRange`; MPL-2.0, read as behaviour only) where the spec is
  silent; node-opcua agrees where noted.
  - *Syntax:* `dimension[,dimension]*`, `dimension = n | n:m`, digits only, each index a `u32`; `n:m` needs `n < m`
    (`3:3` and `5:2` are errors; one element is `3`). Anything else is `BadIndexRangeInvalid`. Bounds: text at most 256
    bytes, at most 16 dimensions (`numeric_range.zig`; open62541 allows 100), so nothing is allocated for an index,
    only for the elements actually selected; all arithmetic is `u64`.
  - *Read:* a range reaching past the end is clipped (§7.27; open62541 clamps too); one that starts past the end, a
    dimension count different from the value's, an empty/null value, or a non-Value attribute is `BadIndexRangeNoData`.
    The result is a `DataValue` with the clipped slice (`dimensions` set for a multi-dimensional array) and the stored
    status and timestamps. A String/ByteString scalar takes a one-dimension range over its bytes; an array of
    Strings/ByteStrings takes one more trailing dimension over the bytes inside each selected element (§7.27 Table 166:
    `0:1,7:9` on `["TestString","Test","String"]` gives `["ing", null]`; only "no element has data" is `NoData`).
    **Known difference:** open62541 `UA_Variant_copyRange` fails the whole request when one element fails; the spec wins.
    Order of checks: attribute id, syntax, data encoding, node (an unknown node wins over a well-formed range).
  - *A scalar that is not a String/ByteString/XmlElement takes no range,* on Read and on Write: the range is not used
    and the whole value is read or written (§7.28 ReadValueId, §5.11.4 Write; node-opcua does the same). **Known
    difference:** open62541 treats a scalar as a one-element array (index `0` reads it, any other is
    `BadIndexRangeNoData`); the LIVE test asserts open62541's answer.
  - *Write:* the range must lie inside the stored array (no growth; `BadIndexRangeNoData`); the new value must have
    exactly as many elements as the range selects, else `BadIndexRangeDataMismatch` (§5.11.4, §7.27). **Known
    difference:** open62541 answers `BadIndexRangeInvalid`; the LIVE test asserts that. A scalar of the right type counts
    as one element; same built-in type as the stored one (`BadTypeMismatch`); nothing stored -> `BadIndexRangeInvalid`.
    Access-level checks keep their precedence. A range on a non-Value attribute is not used. The write is built on a
    copy and swapped in, so every refusal leaves the stored value untouched. Writing into the bytes of String elements
    (one more dimension than the array): one String per selected element, each exactly as wide as the byte range; every
    selected element must contain the range (`NoData`); counts and widths are checked (`DataMismatch`).
  - *Monitored items:* the `IndexRange` of `ItemToMonitor` is parsed at `CreateMonitoredItems` (bad syntax is
    `BadIndexRangeInvalid` for that item) and kept with the item. The initial value and every sample are narrowed by the same code
    as Read, so only the selected part is compared (a change outside the range queues nothing) and reported; a
    range that selects nothing (the array shrank, a non-Value attribute) is sampled as a status-only `BadIndexRangeNoData`
    value, reported once and again when data returns. The range cannot be changed by `ModifyMonitoredItems` (it
    belongs to the monitored target). Behaviour as Read; the spec does not say what a monitored item does when the range
    selects nothing, open62541 and node-opcua report the Bad status as a value.
  - *Limits:* a range with more than 16 dimensions is refused.


## Threat model

**Both halves speak `SecurityPolicy#Basic256Sha256` at Sign and
SignAndEncrypt** (`security.zig`, over the `rsa` module). The server side is
opt-in: `Config.security = null` (the default) keeps it `#None`-only, with
every byte on the wire identical to the pre-security server; setting it to a
`SecurityConfig` (an RSA key pair + application certificate, plus a trust
policy) turns on the whole thing — asymmetric OpenSecureChannel, P-SHA256 key
derivation, per-chunk symmetric sign/encrypt, SecurityToken renewal with an
overlap window, the CreateSession/ActivateSession signature exchange and
RSA-OAEP-encrypted `UserNameIdentityToken`s.

**What security is enforced.**

| Property | Mechanism | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| the peer holds the key it presents | RSA-PKCS1v1.5/SHA-256 signature over the whole OPN message | `BadSecurityChecksFailed` |
| the OPN was meant for *us* | `ReceiverCertificateThumbprint` == SHA-1 of our certificate, constant-time | `BadCertificateInvalid` |
| the peer certificate is well-formed and in date | `std.crypto.Certificate` behind a bounds-checked DER pre-walk + `notBefore`/`notAfter` vs the injected wall clock | `BadCertificateInvalid` / `BadCertificateTimeInvalid` |
| the peer certificate key fits the policy | RSA modulus 2048..4096 bits for `Basic256Sha256` (OPC 10000-7 min/max asymmetric key length; open62541 `rsaNewChannelContext`: 256..512 bytes -> `BadCertificateUseNotAllowed`); the server's own key too | `BadCertificateUseNotAllowed` (peer certificate), `BadSecurityPolicyRejected` (own key); client: `error.KeyLengthOutOfPolicy` before any I/O |
| the peer certificate is *trusted* | caller-supplied `CertificatePolicy.check` | whatever the policy returns |
| only advertised modes are usable | the (policy, mode) pair must appear in `Config.endpoints` | `BadSecurityModeRejected` |
| the nonce carries full entropy | `ClientNonce.len == 32` (the policy's key length) | `BadNonceInvalid` |
| every chunk is authentic | HMAC-SHA256 over the plaintext incl. the MessageHeader; AES-256-CBC under it at SignAndEncrypt | `BadSecurityChecksFailed` |
| a token cannot outlive its lease | `now_ms - created > RevisedLifetime` | `BadSecureChannelTokenUnknown` |
| a renewal does not cut off in-flight messages | the previous token stays valid for `token_renewal_overlap_ms`, capped at its own expiry | `BadSecureChannelTokenUnknown` past the window |
| a renewal cannot change the policy | a `renew` OPN must arrive under the policy the channel was opened with (`#None` → Basic256Sha256 refused; the reverse already was) | `BadSecurityPolicyRejected` |
| a chunk cannot be replayed, reordered or dropped | every authenticated chunk's `SequenceNumber` must be the previous one + 1 (wrap below 1024 once past `UInt32.MaxValue − 1024`, §6.7.2.4); an `issue` OPN starts a new count, a secured `renew` continues it | `BadSecurityChecksFailed` |
| the channel and the session belong together | `ClientSignature` over serverCertificate ‖ serverNonce, verified against the session's `ClientCertificate` | `BadApplicationSignatureInvalid` |
| the session cannot move channels | session is channel-bound; no transfer is implemented | `BadSecureChannelIdInvalid` |
| the client can authenticate *us* | `ServerSignature` over clientCertificate ‖ clientNonce | client-side check |
| the client cannot be fed a replayed response | `Channel.recvService` applies the same `sequenceFollows` rule to every authenticated response chunk; the `issue` OPN response starts the count | `error.SequenceNumberInvalid` (client) |
| a password is not readable or replayable | RSA-OAEP over `UInt32 len ‖ password ‖ serverNonce`, nonce compared constant-time | `BadIdentityTokenInvalid` |
| a policy cannot be downgraded | a plaintext password against a non-`#None` `UserTokenPolicy` is refused | `BadIdentityTokenInvalid` |

Every secret-dependent comparison — thumbprints, nonces, passwords,
authentication tokens, HMAC tags — goes through
`std.crypto.timing_safe` (`security.constantTimeEql`, built on
`timing_safe.compare`, or `timing_safe.eql` for fixed-size arrays). There is
no `std.mem.eql` on a secret anywhere in the security path.

**What is *not* enforced, and must be understood before deploying.**

- **No trust store, no chain walk, no revocation.** The module validates a
  certificate's structure and validity period and then asks
  `SecurityConfig.certificate_policy`; with `certificate_policy = null` it
  accepts any structurally valid, in-date certificate, self-signed included.
  That authenticates the *channel* (the peer proved possession of the key it
  showed) but authenticates no *identity*. A real deployment wires the policy
  to its trust list — e.g. the sibling `x509` module's `verifyChain` against
  the DER files in the server's PKI directory. CRL/OCSP is likewise the
  policy's business. This is a deliberate seam, not an oversight: an OPC UA
  trust list is a deployment artifact, and a library that invented one would
  be wrong everywhere.
- **No `ApplicationUri`-vs-SAN check** (OPC 10000-6 §6.2.3). open62541's
  server does this and answers `BadCertificateUriInvalid`; this one does not.
- **Certificate-time checks are skipped when `Server.wall_clock_epoch == 0`**
  — the caller injected no wall clock, so the server's time base is
  1601-01-01 and there is nothing honest to compare `notBefore`/`notAfter`
  against. Inject a real epoch in production.
- **`SecurityPolicy#None` is still offered** by any endpoint list that
  includes a None endpoint, and at `#None` everything below is true instead:

  - the wire is exactly as unauthenticated and unencrypted as CoAP-over-plain-
    UDP or SNMPv1/v2c — appropriate on an already-trusted OT/industrial LAN
    segment, never over an untrusted network;
  - a `UserNameIdentityToken` travels **in the clear** unless the endpoint
    offers the encrypted policy (`noneEndpointWithEncryptedUserTokens`).
    `Config.users` is empty by default; passwords are compared in constant
    time so a wrong one cannot be found byte-by-byte from response timing, but
    that only removes the timing oracle, not the eavesdropper;
  - `AuthenticationToken`s are 32 random bytes from the caller-supplied
    `std.Random` (pass a real CSPRNG — it is a bearer credential) and are
    compared in constant time, but anyone who can read the wire has them.

- **`Connection.deinit` must be called** on a secured connection: it frees the
  peer certificate copy and `secureZero`s both key sets. It is a no-op on a
  `#None` connection, which is why the callers that predate the security layer
  are still correct.

**Hostile DER is a first-class input**, and the two extraction entry points
take different routes through it. `std.crypto.Certificate`'s reader
indexes without bounds checks and computes element ends without clamping, so
`security.certificateValidity` — which genuinely needs `notBefore`/`notAfter`
— puts a recursive DER well-formedness walk plus a zero-padded scratch copy in
front of it. That guard is the shared **`x509.safe`** helper
(`security.safeCertificate` delegates to `x509.safe.safeCertificate` — three
modules needed the same guard; see `modules/x509/src/safe.zig`).
`security.certificatePublicKey` needs only the `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` and
takes the leaner `x509.spkiOf` instead: it walks the DER with x509's own
bounds-checked decoder, never reaches `std.crypto.Certificate.parse` at all,
and needs no scratch buffer — see `certificatePublicKey`'s own doc comment in
`security.zig` for why the two functions diverge. Either way, a truncated,
mutated or entirely fabricated certificate is `error.InvalidCertificate`; the
tests sweep every prefix and every single-byte mutation of a real certificate
and fuzz arbitrary bytes through both entry points.

**Resource bounds are the other half of the threat model.** A server is
reachable by definition, so every unbounded thing is a DoS surface. Bounded
explicitly, each with a test:

| Bound | Where | Violation |
|---|---|---|
| chunk size | negotiated `receive_buffer_size` | `ERR BadTcpMessageTooLarge`, close |
| chunks per message | negotiated `max_chunk_count` | `ERR BadTcpMessageTooLarge`, close |
| chunks per OpenSecureChannel | one final chunk (§6.7.2; what asyncua sends and open62541 enforces), checked on the MessageHeader before any RSA | `ERR BadTcpMessageTypeInvalid`, close |
| OPN bytes RSA-decrypted before authentication | `SecurityConfig.max_opn_encrypted_len` (4096: ≤ 16 private-key operations at 2048 bits; a real OPN is 512), checked on the clear header before any RSA | `ERR BadTcpMessageTooLarge`, close |
| reassembled size | negotiated `max_message_size` + the caller's buffer | `ERR BadTcpMessageTooLarge`, close |
| response size | `max_chunk_count` | `ServiceFault BadEncodingLimitsExceeded` |
| sessions / subscriptions / monitored items | `Config` | `BadTooManySessions` / `…Subscriptions` / `…MonitoredItems` |
| sessions on one SecureChannel | `Config.max_sessions_per_channel` (4) | `BadTooManySessions` |
| `SessionName` length | `Config.max_session_name_len` (512) | `BadEncodingLimitsExceeded` |
| queued Publish requests | `Config.max_publish_requests` | `BadTooManyPublishRequests` |
| retained notifications (Republish) | `Config.max_retransmission_queue` | oldest dropped |
| continuation points per session | `Config.max_continuation_points` | `BadNoContinuationPoints` |
| operations per request | `Config.max_operations_per_request` — every array-taking service, `Publish` acknowledgements included | `BadTooManyOperations` |
| publishing / sampling interval | `Config.min_*_interval_ms` | revised up |
| publishing cycles per `tick` | `max_cycles_per_tick` | deadline resynchronised |
| type-hierarchy walk depth | `nodestore.max_subtype_depth` | walk stops |

**Session slots are reclaimed when the channel dies, not when it times out.**
A session is pinned to the SecureChannel it was created on, and session
transfer is not implemented, so a session whose channel is gone can never be
used by anyone again. `Server.closeChannelSessions` therefore runs the moment
a channel ends — superseded by a later `OpenSecureChannel(issue)`, closed by
`CLO`, aborted with an `ERR`, or dropped by the driver via
`Connection.deinit` — instead of leaving the slot pinned for a
client-requested `RevisedSessionTimeout` (up to `max_session_timeout_ms`,
600 s). `RevisedSessionTimeout` (`Server.expireSessions`, driven from
`Connection.tick`) remains the bound for a channel that is still alive but
idle; `max_sessions_per_channel` bounds what one live channel may hold at
once, so a single unauthenticated socket cannot take the whole
`max_sessions` pool. **A driver must call `Connection.deinit` when the socket
goes away** — that is the only reclamation path for a peer that simply
vanishes.

Continuation points are **session-scoped**: a handle from another session (or
a guessed one) is `BadContinuationPointInvalid`, never someone else's cursor.
Sessions are **channel-bound**: a request replaying a valid AuthenticationToken
on a different SecureChannel is `BadSecureChannelIdInvalid` (session transfer
between channels is not implemented, which closes that door rather than
opening it half-way).
**Residual risk:** `Config.max_lifetime_count` (the ceiling on a granted `LifetimeCount`) below three keep-alive
counts silently overrides §5.13.2's floor (`server.zig`, `@min(raw, cfg.max_lifetime_count)` after the
floor); it is an operator setting, not peer input.


## Codec-only vs driven

Everything in `encoding` and `services` is a codec; what makes it *driven* is
whether a state machine in `root` (client) or `server` (server) uses it.

- **Driven, both directions, at `#None` *and* `Basic256Sha256`
  Sign/SignAndEncrypt:** OpenSecureChannel (issue and renew)/CloseSecureChannel,
  GetEndpoints, FindServers, CreateSession, ActivateSession, CloseSession,
  Read, Write, Browse, BrowseNext, TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIds, Call,
  CreateSubscription, ModifySubscription, SetPublishingMode, DeleteSubscriptions,
  CreateMonitoredItems, ModifyMonitoredItems, SetMonitoringMode,
  DeleteMonitoredItems, Publish, Republish.

- **Codec-only** (structures encode/decode, nothing drives them):
  `EventNotificationList`/`EventFieldList` (no server-side event model),
  `StatusChangeNotification` on the client side, `DiagnosticInfo` trees
  (always encoded empty), `SignedSoftwareCertificate`, `X509IdentityToken`
  and `IssuedIdentityToken` type ids, `ActivateSessionRequest.
  UserTokenSignature` (decoded, never required — it only matters for the
  X509/Issued tokens, which are not implemented), and
  `SecurityPolicy.aes256_sha256_rsapss` (an enum value + `uri()` only).

## Verification

Run `scripts/modtest opcua` (add `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast` for the optimised-build probes). The LIVE tests need a
container runtime (`podman`) and skip loudly when it or the port is unavailable. The tests of our client against an
open62541 *server* publish the container's 4840 on an ephemeral loopback port, under a container name made of the
process id and that port, so two runs at once do not share either; readiness is the server's own "listening" log line (a
published port accepts connections before the server is up). The tests of open62541's *clients* against our server
keep the port 4840 (the image's example clients dial it without arguments) and a process-unique container name: a second
run at once finds the port taken and skips loudly instead of failing.

- **Offline:** RFC/spec-shaped round-trips for every built-in type, transport framing, secure-channel KATs,
  address-space unit tests, and an end-to-end suite that drives the *server* with the module's own *client* encoder
  over an in-memory pipe (both halves must agree on bytes, not just on structs); the client's `SecureChannel`,
  `Session` and `Subscription` against `Connection` over that pipe at `#None` and at SignAndEncrypt, and scripted-peer
  tests for answers a real server would not give (surplus or failed results, an answer for another channel, an empty
  nonce, a CreateSession answer signed with another key).
- **Hostile input:** oversize chunk, chunk count over the negotiated maximum, abort chunk mid-message, message-size/type
  violations, reserved NodeId encoding byte, ExtensionObject body length overrun, continuation point from another
  session, publish acknowledgement for an unknown sequence number, MSG before OPN, wrong TokenId, rejected security
  policy — each asserted to produce a typed error/fault, never a crash or a hang. Plus `std.testing.fuzz` feeding
  arbitrary bytes into `feed`/`tick`.
- **Hostile security input** (each a specific `Bad…` status and a closed channel rather than a polite answer): a flipped
  bit in the chunk-type byte / SecureChannelId / ciphertext, a chunk sealed with the wrong keys, a correctly-MAC'd chunk
  with a `PaddingSize` pointing past the message, an expired SecurityToken, the previous token used past its renewal
  overlap, an OPN addressed to another server's certificate, a wrong-length nonce, an unadvertised SecurityMode, a
  certificate the trust policy rejects, a certificate outside its validity window, an absent / stale-nonce /
  foreign-key `ClientSignature`, a `CreateSession` presenting a certificate other than the channel's, a session
  replayed on a second channel, a replayed encrypted password, a replayed MSG chunk, a `#None` channel renewed under
  Basic256Sha256, a plaintext password against an encrypted `UserTokenPolicy`, certificate keys at the edges of the
  per-policy band. Certificate parsing additionally gets every prefix of a real certificate, every single-byte
  mutation of one, hand-built malformed DER, and `std.testing.fuzz`.
- **Fuzz:** `OPCUA_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` through testkit's deterministic driver (`_ONLY` selects a harness).
  Harnesses: `opcua-session` (a recorded client conversation at `#None`) and `opcua-secure` (at Basic256Sha256
  SignAndEncrypt), each replayed with one chunk damaged / dropped / duplicated / swapped / replaced, a rig per run
  (`server.zig`); `opcua-range` (a live session reading and writing ranged values against a model of an `Int32[5]`
  re-derived from the grammar, structured and byte-edited ranges, reach labels counted in the plain test lane); the DER
  harness and `fuzzConnection` (`fuzz_test.zig`).
- **Live (the real oracle):**
  - *their client -> our server:* open62541's stock `tutorial_client_firststeps`, `client_subscription_loop`, `client`
    (GetEndpoints on its own connection, username login, Browse, Read/Write of a String NodeId, subscription, method
    Call) and `client_encryption` (picks our SignAndEncrypt endpoint out of `GetEndpoints` itself), run from
    `docker.io/open62541/open62541` with `--network host` (process-unique container names); their stdout is the assertion;
  - *our client -> their server:* a real `server_ctt`, including Basic256Sha256 Sign and SignAndEncrypt, client-side
    renewal, `translateBrowsePaths`, `modifyMonitoredItems`, `setMonitoringMode`, and ranged reads/writes of its Demo
    Int32 scalar, `Int32[10]` and `Int32[3][3]` (one table compared as a whole; the lines marked KNOWN DIFFERENCE are
    where this module answers otherwise, see NumericRange above);
  - *our client -> our server:* over a real loopback socket, the server driven from a second thread.
- **Replayed third-party interop, hermetic** (`src/asyncua_replay.zig` over `src/testdata/asyncua_transcript.txt`): the
  whole recorded Python **`asyncua`** exchange, re-executed with no interpreter, no `asyncua`, no child process and no
  socket. asyncua generates its own throwaway RSA-2048 certificate and makes seven connections — GetEndpoints at
  `#None` before each secured session, one session at Basic256Sha256 / SignAndEncrypt (browse the Objects folder,
  read and write `ns=1;s=the.answer`, call a method, receive subscription notifications), one at Sign with a
  Basic256Sha256-encrypted `UserNameIdentityToken`, and one holding a 10 s SecurityToken while reading every second for
  30 s, which forces real mid-stream renewals across the overlap window. The replay feeds every recorded client
  datagram back in at its recorded `t=` and requires this server to answer with **exactly the recorded bytes**, then
  re-derives each connection's policy/mode, walks the opc.tcp framing of both directions (no `ERR`, at least three
  `OPN` on the renewal channel), decodes the `GetEndpointsResponse` and requires our three endpoints with our own
  certificate on the secured two, and checks `the.answer` ended at the value asyncua wrote.
  What makes it replayable is what the module already had: `Server.init` takes the `std.Random` it draws from (one
  seeded `DefaultCsprng` produces the RSA key pair, the certificate, every nonce, token id and AuthenticationToken, in
  a fixed draw order), and `feed`/`tick` take `now_ms` with `wall_clock_epoch` fixing the wall clock's zero. What it
  cannot carry: it cannot discover a NEW divergence (the peer's bytes are frozen at one asyncua release); it cannot
  tell "we broke interop" from "we changed valid bytes" (a different nonce draw or a reordered endpoint list fails it
  with no peer having refused anything: a red replay is a summons to re-run `zig build interop-opcua`, not a verdict);
  it cannot prove asyncua ACCEPTS what we send; and asyncua's own assertions and exit status were checked when the
  transcript was taken and are kept in the file as `#` notes.
- **Live, outside the module** (`zig build interop-opcua`, needs a Python with `asyncua` + `cryptography`; `-- --capture`
  rewrites the transcript): `tools/asyncua_driver.py` driving this server for real. The only half that can find a new
  divergence, and a pre-release check; the replay is the per-commit one. `zig build check-interop` compiles it on every
  lane so the instrument cannot rot.
- **Basic256Sha256 goldens** (`server_interop.zig`): *self-derived*, labelled as such — a full asymmetric
  `OpenSecureChannel` message (from a fixed key seed and a fixed OAEP seed, so `rsa.generate`, `rsa.selfSignedCert`,
  RSA-OAEP and RSA-PKCS1v1.5 are pinned byte for byte) and one MSG chunk at each of Sign and SignAndEncrypt, each
  re-encoded and re-opened identically; *captured* from a real `open62541 server_ctt` — the OPN request and response of
  a live Sign handshake (real certificates cross-checked against each other's thumbprints; the encrypted region is
  asserted opaque and block-aligned, since decrypting it needs an ephemeral key this repository does not persist) and
  one Read request/response MSG chunk at each of Sign and SignAndEncrypt, decoded, decrypted, verified and re-encoded
  byte-identically with the session keys that exchange derived. No live capture triggered multi-chunk secured framing;
  `server.zig`'s multi-chunk-secured-Browse test covers it self-derived. **Key derivation KAT:** `deriveKeys` over two
  fixed 32-byte nonces against bytes computed by an independent Python implementation of RFC 5246 §5's P_hash with
  SHA-256; `pSha256` itself is anchored by the published TLS-1.2 PRF/SHA-256 vector, and the layout (which slice is
  which key) is cross-checked by the live interop.
- **`#None` goldens** cut from live traffic (`OPCUA_CAPTURE_DIR=… zig build test-opcua` dumps the raw streams): Hello,
  OpenSecureChannel, GetEndpoints, CreateSession, ActivateSession, Read, Browse, CreateSubscription,
  CreateMonitoredItems and an acknowledging Publish request are **captured** open62541 bytes; the ACK, OPN response,
  GetEndpoints/Read/Publish responses are **self-derived** (this server's encoder) and labelled so in the source. Each
  decodes and re-encodes byte-identically; all are anonymised (loopback addresses only, no certificates, no device
  identities).
- **Wireshark cross-check** (one-off): the captured messages were framed as pcap-style records and dissected with
  `rawshark -d proto:opcua`; none was `_ws.malformed`, and the dissector read this server's own fields correctly.
- **Stack probe** (`stackprobe_test.zig`, ReleaseFast only) and **ctgrind** (`ctgrind_harness.zig`, not in the test
  lane): channel nonces through `deriveKeys` leave 0 contexts, keys and body through sign/encrypt and decrypt/verify
  leave the HMAC verdict and the post-MAC padding/length handling (see the card's `**Hardening:**` line). The probe does
  not reach the paths that need a live peer (Backlog).
- **Mutation:** the optimised-build probes alone see the wipes of freed key material (`Allocator.free` poisons the block
  in Debug and ReleaseSafe); those mutants are argued UNOBSERVABLE, not tested.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and
  the delta runs after it.


## What is deliberately not done

Server side, deliberately out of scope for this part — each is a Bad status, never a silent partial answer:

- **Security policies other than `#None` and `Basic256Sha256`:** no `Basic128Rsa15`, no `Basic256` (both deprecated), no
  `Aes128Sha256RsaOaep`, no `Aes256Sha256RsaPss` (an enum value + URI only). Any OPN naming one is
  `BadSecurityPolicyRejected`. The newer two are wanted (Backlog).
- **Identity tokens:** no `X509IdentityToken`, no `IssuedIdentityToken` (`BadIdentityTokenInvalid`) — and therefore no
  `UserTokenSignature` verification, which is what those tokens need.
- **PKI:** no trust store, no chain building, no CRL/OCSP, no `ApplicationUri`-vs-SAN matching — see the threat model;
  the accept/reject verdict is the caller's `CertificatePolicy`. A library that invented a trust list would be wrong
  everywhere.
- **Filters:** a `DataChangeFilter` is applied (see below); an event filter (or any other filter type) on a monitored item is
  `BadMonitoredItemFilterUnsupported`, and therefore no events, no `EventNotificationList` production, no alarms & conditions (Backlog).
- **DataChangeFilter** (OPC 10000-4 §7.22.2, `server.zig`). `ItemToMonitor` with a `DataChangeFilter` (ExtensionObject id 724: Trigger,
  DeadbandType, DeadbandValue; applied on create and on `ModifyMonitoredItems`, which replaces the old filter). Trigger `Status` reports only a
  status change, `StatusValue` (the default without a filter) a status or value change, `StatusValueTimestamp` also a change of the source
  timestamp. An **absolute** deadband applies to a numeric Value (Byte..Double scalars and arrays of them): a change is reported when it is
  *more* than the deadband away from the **last reported** value (a NaN difference counts; any element of an array; a length change),
  the first value is always reported. Refusals per item: a deadband on a non-numeric Value or another attribute `BadFilterNotAllowed`, a
  negative or non-finite deadband or an unknown DeadbandType `BadDeadbandFilterInvalid`, an unknown Trigger or a body that is not 16 octets
  `BadMonitoredItemFilterInvalid`. A **percent** deadband (OPC 10000-8 §6.4.2) is `percent / 100 * (high - low)` of the variable's
  EURange and applies to analog variables only: the store models the range (`VariableAttributes.eu_range`, set by `addVariable`'s
  `eu_range`, which with `eu_range_node_id` also adds the `EURange` HasProperty node, DataType Range `i=884`, for clients); a variable
  without one is refused `BadFilterNotAllowed` (Part 8: it "applies only to AnalogItems with an EURange"; the specification names no
  code for a missing range, this one is the one used for a filter the node cannot take), a percent outside 0..100 `BadDeadbandFilterInvalid`.
  The absolute width is fixed when the item is created or modified (a later change of the range is not followed).
  open62541 and node-opcua offer the same trigger/absolute/percent set.
- **HistoryRead** (OPC 10000-4 §5.10.3): the store keeps no history; `Config.history` is the seam to a historian
  (`HistoryProvider`: `read_raw`, optional `read_at_time`, `release_continuation`; open62541's `UA_HistoryDatabase` has the same shape).
  The server decodes `ReadRawModifiedDetails` and `ReadAtTimeDetails`, checks per node that it is a Variable with the `HistoryRead`
  user access bit, the data encoding and the details (both bounds unspecified, or one unspecified without a value count, is
  `BadHistoryOperationInvalid`; `isReadModified` is `BadHistoryOperationUnsupported`: no store of modifications), asks the provider and
  answers `HistoryData`; empty is `BadNoData`, and `Config.max_history_values_per_node` (1000) caps one answer, the rest waiting behind
  the provider's opaque ContinuationPoint, which `releaseContinuationPoints` hands back to it. `TimestampsToReturn` selects among the
  stored timestamps. Without a provider every node answers `BadHistoryOperationUnsupported`. Not built: processed (aggregate) reads,
  event history, `HistoryUpdate`.
- **Node management:** no AddNodes/AddReferences/DeleteNodes/DeleteReferences (`BadServiceUnsupported`) — the address
  space is built by the host program, not over the wire (Backlog).
- **Other service sets:** no Query, no HistoryUpdate, no processed or event history, no RegisterNodes/UnregisterNodes, no
  RegisterServer, no session transfer between channels, no `TransferSubscriptions`, no Views (a non-null ViewId is
  `BadViewIdUnknown`), no `DataEncoding` other than Default Binary, no reverse-connect, no discovery server
  registration, no multi-server namespaces (`ExpandedNodeId.server_index` is decoded, never resolved).
- **Address space:** the seeded namespace 0 is the browsable *skeleton*, not the full ~2000-node standard nodeset (a
  generated NodeSet2 artifact; Backlog); no ModellingRules, no `Argument` metadata on Method nodes (a Call's arguments
  are validated by the method implementation itself), no `DataTypeDefinition`/`RolePermissions`/`AccessRestrictions`
  attributes.
- **Interleaving:** one message at a time per connection (a second chunk run interleaved with an unfinished one is
  `BadTcpMessageTypeInvalid`); a response is never sent in chunks smaller than the negotiated buffer minus its own
  framing.
- **Client side:** no `Variant` `ArrayDimensions` reshaping (multi-dimensional arrays stay flat).


## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle MIXED

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle MIXED** — anchored for some paths, self for others — the evidence below names which.

**What the tests actually contain.** P-SHA256/AES KAT EXTERNAL; binary framing self round-trip; open62541 interop skips if unreachable

## Backlog / deferred

- **Burn depths of the live paths are unmeasured**: `SecureChannel.open` (32 KiB), every `Session`/`Subscription` method and `Connection.tick` (128 KiB) need a live peer, so `stackprobe_test.zig` does not reach them; the sizes are margins. Also `deriveKeys` still returns `ChannelKeys` by value and `services.zig`/`server.zig` copy `SecurityContext`/`ChannelKeys` by value (`ch.security.?`, `c.keys orelse`) inside those burned frames. Next: drive one Basic256Sha256 session over the loopback fixture under the probe, then move the copies to pointers.
- **Security policies `Aes128Sha256RsaOaep` / `Aes256Sha256RsaPss`** (survey): `Basic256Sha256` is deprecated in OPC UA 1.05 and new servers may offer only the newer policies; medium, fits §2 (sibling `rsa` has PSS/OAEP *(inferred)*).
- **Events and alarms & conditions** (survey): the `EventFilter` on monitored items, `EventNotificationList`, the event type model and conditions (OPC 10000-9); large, fits §2.
- **Full standard NodeSet + node management + PubSub (Part 14)** (survey): large, fits §2 for NodeSet (generated data); PubSub is a project of its own.
